text: The next two hours. <break time="0.8s" /> Flew by on rosy wings. <break time="0.8s" /> Della searched every store in town. <break time="0.8s" /> For Jims present. <break time="0.8s" /> At last she found it. <break time="0.8s" /> And it surely had been made. <break time="0.8s" /> For Jim and no one else. <break time="0.8s" /> It was a platinum chain. <break time="0.8s" /> For his watch. <break time="0.8s" /> Simple and plain in design. <break time="0.8s" /> It was like Jim himself. <break time="0.8s" /> Quiet and valuable. <break time="0.8s" /> She paid twenty one dollars for it. <break time="0.8s" /> And hurried home. <break time="0.8s" /> With the eighty seven cents. <break time="0.8s" /> With that chain on his watch. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim could check the time proudly. <break time="0.8s" /> In any company. <break time="0.8s" /> Grand as the watch was he sometimes looked at it secretly. <break time="0.8s" /> Because of the old leather strap. <break time="0.8s" /> He used instead of a chain. <break time="0.8s" /> When Della reached home. <break time="0.8s" /> She got out her curling irons. <break time="0.8s" /> And went to work. <break time="0.8s" /> Within forty minutes. <break time="0.8s" /> Her head was covered. <break time="0.8s" /> With tiny, close lying curls. <break time="0.8s" /> She looked at herself. <break time="0.8s" /> In the mirror. <break time="0.8s" /> Long and carefully. <break time="0.8s" /> Jim will say. <break time="0.8s" /> I look like a schoolboy. <break time="0.8s" /> She worried.
